solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quietly, set for recreation

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction meaning softly
to set something down is to lay it

explanation.surface: Something is quietly arranged as a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Play is leisure activity done for enjoyment, the same as recreation.

clue.text: Moved up prior to creating miscellany

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was promoted before putting together a mixed collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' looks like part of 'moved up', a promotion, but it is the anagram signal working on UP PRIOR TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixed assortment of things, literally or figuratively, so it is a miscellany.

clue.text: A king, in dread, unable to sleep?

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces are placed inside the word for dread

parts.note: awe is reverential fear or dread
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch lies sleepless with fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wide awake is conscious and cannot drift off, hence the question mark on a playful definition.

clue.text: We hear flower placed where there was a small population

definitions.text: where there was a small population

indicators.note: We hear says the words are to be taken by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a lily is a flower and put means placed

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a bloom has been set down where few people lived.
explanation.walkthrough: Lilliput is the island of tiny people in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lilliputians are only inches tall, so the island's population is small in a literal, physical sense.

clue.text: Prisoner at home with companion

parts.note: someone at home is in
a mate is a friend or companion

explanation.surface: A jailbird is at home with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is someone confined in a prison or institution.

clue.text: Slip from circuit, set incomplete

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

indicators.note: incomplete says the word set loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: A runner slips off a track while a set goes unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a small error or failure of concentration, a slip.

clue.text: Ancient king's even-handed letter read out?

indicators.note: read out says the words are to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: even-handed means fair, and O is a letter

explanation.surface: An old monarch has a fair-minded letter recited publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was a ruler of ancient Egypt, so an ancient king.

clue.text: Periodically stroke part of foot

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth and sixth of stroke

explanation.surface: Every so often someone strokes a part of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe is one of the digits at the front of the foot.

clue.text: Doctor got up in a bad mood

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor
rose means got up

explanation.surface: A doctor gets out of bed grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes a sullen, gloomy temper, a bad mood.

clue.text: Side hugging Aussie skipper in cafe

indicators.note: hugging says the side wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a kangaroo, or roo, skips about in Australia

explanation.surface: A sports team embraces Australia's captain in a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' looks like a team captain, matching 'Side', but it is a hopping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom is a small restaurant serving tea and light meals, a café.

clue.text: Head going around left piece of crockery

indicators.note: going around says the word for head encloses the other letter

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A head turns around a piece of left-behind china.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a flat dish, one item of crockery.

clue.text: Love of French poetry

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Someone loves French verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, so an example of poetry.

clue.text: Alert, showing leg before the dance

indicators.note: before places the leg piece ahead of the rest

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone sharp shows off a leg ahead of the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket field's leg side, the side the batsman's legs point to, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball is an idiom for being quick-witted and attentive.

clue.text: Green piles of hay in lots of five lines?

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
ricks are stacks of hay

explanation.surface: Green haystacks are set out in five rows.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is a comic poem of five lines, so several of them are lots of five-line verses.

clue.text: Chap wandering around yonder

indicators.note: wandering around says the letters of the next word stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A man is roaming about over there.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodney is also this puzzle's setter, a little joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodney is a man's name, and crosswords freely define male names as chap.

clue.text: State ad must be prepared for computer file

indicators.note: must be prepared says the letters have to be made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A government advert has to be readied for storing digitally.
explanation.definitionFit: A data set is a collection of related records held together, typically as one computer file.

clue.text: Football team taking some frightful hammering

indicators.note: taking some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A football club suffers a dreadful thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulham is a London club in English professional football.

clue.text: Cruel keeping some chipmunk indoors

indicators.note: keeping some says the answer is a run of letters held inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: It is heartless to keep a chipmunk shut inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Cruel keeping' as the definition, but 'keeping' belongs with 'some' as the hiding signal; 'Cruel' alone means unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel and unkind are synonyms, both describing behaviour that causes others distress.

clue.text: Polish artist is a female

parts.note: to sand is to smooth or polish
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist from Poland turns out to be a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' masquerades as the nationality; it is the verb to polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a woman's name, so it names a female.

clue.text: Kind heart turning ignorant

indicators.note: turning says the letters of the words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted person grows unaware.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for knowing nothing about something, uninformed.

clue.text: Ogle nice boy, one you clasp, finally

indicators.note: finally says to take the last letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a pleasant lad they would like to embrace at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye someone up is to look them over with obvious interest, as ogling does.

clue.text: Moan when end falls off auto

indicators.note: when end falls off says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to carp is to grumble or moan

explanation.surface: Someone complains when a piece falls off their vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is short for automobile, a motor car.

clue.text: Approached large creature in desert?

parts.note: came means approached or drew near
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big animal drew near in the wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is the classic animal of sandy wastes, so an example of a desert creature.

clue.text: I sell new cotton fabric

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A trader advertises fresh cotton cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread and the cloth knitted from it, used for stockings.

clue.text: Boy's fast, but failing to finish

indicators.note: failing to finish says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A lad is quick but does not complete the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, but it is the religious fast of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Len is a short form of the man's name Leonard, so crosswords treat it as a boy.

clue.text: Large number nabbed by detectives. returning with powerful force

indicators.note: returning says the whole built piece is read backwards
nabbed by says the number is caught inside the detectives

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
many is a large number

explanation.surface: Many crooks are caught by police coming back in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nabbed by' gives CIMANYD, which 'returning' reads backwards; the full stop before 'returning' is surface punctuation only.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means energetic and forceful, full of vigorous power.

clue.text: Takes pen to rewrite online language?

indicators.note: to rewrite says the letters are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a pen to redraft something meant for the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Netspeak is the jargon and abbreviated style used in internet chat and messaging.

clue.text: Regrettably, a girl can only be heard

indicators.note: can only be heard says the words count by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Sadly, a young woman is audible but invisible.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of sorrow, used as a sentence adverb meaning unfortunately.
